groups.trust_reason: Verification runs on the same route class as the data inside the user's kernel; any surface only displays the result, and a hosted surface may run it only on a route eligible for the data label.
Citations come from the kernel's versioned source manifest; clicking is a UI action on every surface, resolved by the kernel.
Document intelligence reads private files, so it runs in the local kernel (companion or desktop) with files mounted read-only; hosted web only for data the organisation owns and attests.
These are the privacy controls themselves: enforced by the kernel outside the model, so no surface may bypass or weaken them; surfaces only render and relay the user's decision.
Helpers that advise; enforcement stays with labels, grants and the sandbox. Run in the kernel so detection never needs a third-party processor.
Workbench features that need local files, processes, snapshots and the OS; the web companion shows them through the kernel API where the browser is only the screen.
Memory lives in the encrypted local vault owned by the kernel; every surface reads and edits it through the kernel with the same labels and recovery rules.

Capsule issuance, selective release and signed comments are produced by the kernel's release pipeline and checked by the recipient; approval is only on a trusted path (native window or terminal), never the page.
The recipient view must need no install: a static page that verifies in the browser with no upload, so the recipient trusts nothing the sender hosts.
Zero-knowledge proof of a private calculation is a research go/no-go (D34); not claimable until a verified construction exists.
Attestation and signature checks must run in the user's own kernel, never be taken from a page or a server's say-so; surfaces display the verified facts.
Deferred until the underlying service or contract path is verified; no claim until then.
Local audio and embedding models need device compute and microphone permission under native consent; the web companion cannot grant them safely.
Optional sign-in is an account concern of hosted mode only; local mode needs no account.
